title: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) for the Partition of India
summary: On 3 June 1947 the British government and Viceroy Lord Mountbatten announced, with Nehru and Jinnah, a plan to end British rule by dividing British India into India and Pakistan. Provincial assemblies would vote on partition, boundary commissions would draw the lines, and Sylhet would hold a referendum. Power passed a year earlier than first planned.

uncertainty.note: Date of the announcement in London and New Delhi.

as_recorded.value: Tuesday 3 June 1947 (Hansard, Commons and Lords statements)
On the 3 June 1947 he stunned everyone by announcing with leaders Jawaharlal Nehru and Muhammad Ali Jinnah

where.historical_name: New Delhi, seat of the Viceroy of India, British Indian Empire

importance.justification: Set the terms of the partition of British India and the independence of India and Pakistan, with mass displacement and violence following.

related.because: The plan fixed the creation of two dominions and brought forward the transfer of power to August 1947.
